title: Homage, Remembrance, and Prayer
program_note:
Homage, Remembrance, and Prayer began as an homage to Samuel Adler—who was my principal composition teacher at The Eastman School of Music—on his 75th birthday in March, 2003.  Near the beginning of the piece it presents a musical “signature” of the letters in Adler's name:  A-D-L (La, or A) -E-R (Re, or D), and S (Es, or E-flat) -A-M (Mi, or E-natural) -U (Ut, or C) -E-L (La, or A).

Since I wrote this piece in early March, 2003, the impending war in Iraq was on my mind.  As I was working with this musical signature, I noticed that it bore a similarity to a setting of the words “Oseh Shalom Bimromav” from the Jewish liturgy—words which represent the hope for peace.  Curiously, though, the melody also bears a similarity to another musical signature—that of 9/11/2001 (where 0 represents C, 1 represents C-sharp, etc.; 9-1-1-2-0-0-1 would therefore be represented by A-C-sharp-C-sharp-D-C-C-C-sharp).  I brought all three of these melodic snippets together, into a piece which arcs from the relative calm of ADLER, to the anxiety of the tragic events of 9-1-1, and ends with the beauty and true calm of Oseh Shalom.  It thus ends with a prayer:  “May God who brings peace to the universe bring peace to us and to all people.  And let us say:  Amen.”  Since peace is not yet upon us, however, the setting of the word “Amen” is omitted, leaving us hanging both emotionally and musically.
